title: Document Ingestion Requested (v1)
description: Requests that a previously uploaded Document be ingested. Published by Laravel via the transactional outbox (ADR-0008) after a Document transitions from UPLOADED to QUEUED (ADR-0007), and consumed by the Python ingestion worker.

event_id.description: Stable logical identifier for this ingestion request. Does not change across publication retries or duplicate SQS delivery; consumers must use this, not the SQS transport message identifier, to detect duplicates (ADR-0008).

event_type.description: Fixed discriminator identifying this event's meaning, independent of its version.

event_version.description: Contract version this payload conforms to. A breaking change to this event introduces a new integer version and a new vN.schema.json rather than changing this schema in place. Consumers must reject a version they do not support rather than guess at compatibility.

occurred_at.description: When the ingestion request was recorded (the Document's UPLOADED -> QUEUED transition), not when it was published or received.

workspace_id.description: The immutable public identifier of the owning workspace (ADR-0006). Required so the consumer can preserve tenant context without trusting anything else in the message to imply it.

document_id.description: The immutable public identifier of the Document this request concerns (ADR-0007). This is the aggregate identifier the consumer acts on.

storage_bucket.description: The S3-compatible bucket holding the Document's source content.

storage_key.description: The server-controlled object key for the Document's source content within storage_bucket.

media_type.description: The Document's declared media type, as recorded at upload completion.

byte_size.description: The Document's positive verified size in bytes, as recorded at upload completion. Empty source objects are not eligible for ingestion.

correlation_id.description: Connects the originating HTTP request, the outbox record, this event and downstream logs. Distinct from event_id: correlation_id traces one causal chain across services, event_id identifies one logical ingestion request and drives idempotency.
